reason: This passage (Exodus 2:1-10) is a narrative account of the birth and early life of Moses. It describes a man from the house of Levi marrying a Levite woman, her bearing a son, hiding him for three months, and ultimately placing him in a basket in the Nile River where Pharaoh's daughter finds and raises him. Yahweh (God) does not appear in this text at all, and there are no complaints expressed by any party. The passage contains no divine speech or divine complaints about the people.
